Sourcing Current Climatic Conditions and Fruit Impact

The table summarizes the relationship between climatic conditions, banana fruit characteristics, and pest and disease pressure across all LATAM Sourcing Regions.

Green = Positive Impact | Red = Negative Impact
Climatic Conditions Fruit Condition Pest & Diseases / Agronomic Notes
COLD AND DRY
 Shorter, Lower grade (thinner), Lighter, higher finger count, higher curvature. Decreased Sigatoka and Rots pressure
COLD AND RAINY
 Shorter, Lower grade (thinner), Lighter, higher finger count, higher curvature. Increased Sigatoka and Rots Pressure / Reduced spray window
WARM AND RAINY
 Longer, higher grade (thicker), Heavier, lower finger count, low curvature. Increased Sigatoka and Rots Pressure / Reduced spray window
WARM AND DRY
 Longer, higher grade (thicker), Heavier, lower finger count, low curvature. Decreased Sigatoka and Rots pressure
WARM AND OVERCAST HEAVY RAIN
 Shorter, lower grade (thinner), lighter, intermediate curvature, higher finger count. Reduced spray windows, and reduced photosynthesis.
HOT AND RAINY
 Longer, higher grade (thicker), Heavier, lower finger count, low curvature. Increased Sigatoka and Rots Pressure / Reduced spray window
HOT AND DRY
 Shorter, Lower grade (thinner), Lighter, higher finger count, higher curvature. Decreased Sigatoka and Rots pressure
Standardized Nomenclature

The locked climate palette

Seven conditions, seven colors. Every label is written temperature-first — temperature (Cold / Warm / Hot), then moisture (Dry / Rainy) — so the language stays consistent across every region and every chart.

"Climate drives fruit development. Know the season, anticipate the fruit."
